introParas: Delhi is the capital city of India, located in the northern part of the country. It is one of the most prominent and historically significant cities, known for its rich cultural heritage, iconic landmarks, and vibrant lifestyle. Delhi beautifully blends ancient history with modern development, making it a must-visit destination for travelers.

The city is home to famous attractions like the Red Fort, India Gate, Qutub Minar, and Lotus Temple. Many travelers explore the city through a Delhi Darshan tour by car, which offers a convenient way to visit multiple attractions in a single day. For those with limited time, a Delhi same-day tour is a popular option. With Nuab Tourism, you can enjoy a well-planned and comfortable journey, ensuring you experience the best of Delhi without any hassle.

attractions.name: Red Fort
attractions.text: The Red Fort is one of Delhi’s most iconic historical landmarks, built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Made of red sandstone, this magnificent fort served as the main residence of Mughal rulers for many years. It showcases stunning architecture, beautiful gardens, and rich history, making it a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a must-visit attraction during a Delhi Darshan tour.

attractions.name: India Gate
attractions.text: India Gate is a famous war memorial located in the heart of Delhi. It was built in honor of Indian soldiers who sacrificed their lives during World War I. Surrounded by lush green lawns, it is a popular spot for tourists and locals, especially in the evening when the monument is beautifully illuminated.

attractions.name: Qutub Minar
attractions.text: Qutub Minar is the tallest brick minaret in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built in the 12th century, it reflects Indo-Islamic architecture and stands as a symbol of Delhi’s rich past. The surrounding Qutub complex also features ancient ruins and historical structures.

attractions.name: Lotus Temple
attractions.text: The Lotus Temple is a unique architectural marvel shaped like a blooming lotus flower. It is a Bahá’í House of Worship, open to people of all religions. Known for its peaceful ambiance and stunning design, it is one of the most visited landmarks in Delhi.

attractions.name: Humayun’s Tomb
attractions.text: Humayun’s Tomb is another UNESCO World Heritage Site and a fine example of Mughal architecture. It is the tomb of Emperor Humayun and is believed to have inspired the design of the Taj Mahal. The monument is surrounded by well-maintained gardens, offering a serene atmosphere.

attractions.name: Raj Ghat
attractions.text: Raj Ghat is a memorial dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation. It is a simple yet powerful site where visitors pay tribute to his legacy. The peaceful surroundings make it a place for reflection and respect.

attractions.name: Amber Fort (Amer Fort)
attractions.text: Majestic fort located on a hilltop with sweeping views. Famous for its artistic Hindu architecture and the Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace).

attractions.name: City Palace
attractions.text: A beautiful blend of Mughal and Rajput architecture. Houses museums, courtyards, and the royal family’s residence.

attractions.name: Nahargarh Fort
attractions.text: Perched on a ridge of the Aravalli Hills, this fort offers breathtaking panoramic views of the entire Jaipur city, especially at sunset. It was a formidable defense post and is known for the stunning architecture within, including twelve identical boudoirs for the king’s queens.

attractions.name: Jantar Mantar
attractions.text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest and best-preserved astronomical observatories in the world. Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, who was a scholar of astronomy, it houses a collection of 19 large instruments, including the world’s largest stone sundial.

attractions.name: Jal Mahal (Water Palace)
attractions.text: A beautiful low-rise palace that appears to float in the middle of the Man Sagar Lake, making it a picturesque sight.

attractions.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
attractions.text: Arguably the most iconic landmark of the city, this five-story palace was built in 1799. Its unique honeycomb-like facade has 953 small windows (jharokhas), which allowed the royal ladies to observe the street life below without being seen themselves.

attractions.name: Birla Mandir, Jaipur
attractions.text: Dedicated to Lord Vishnu (Narayan) and his consort Goddess Lakshmi, this modern temple is often referred to as the Laxmi Narayan Temple. It is part of a series of grand temples built by the wealthy Birla family across India.

car.introHeading: Two Holy Cities of the Ganga in a Single Day
introParas: Haridwar and Rishikesh are two of the most revered spiritual destinations in India, sitting on the banks of the sacred River Ganga at the foothills of the Himalayas in Uttarakhand. Haridwar, meaning the “Gateway to God,” is famous for the evening Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri, its ancient temples and its deeply devotional atmosphere. Just a short drive away, Rishikesh is known worldwide as the “Yoga Capital of the World,” celebrated for its iconic suspension bridges, riverside ashrams and serene Ganga ghats. With Nuab Tourism’s private same-day car tour, you can witness both cities in a single, well-planned day — travelling in a clean, air-conditioned vehicle with an experienced driver who knows the route well.
notes: Note: Some temples and ropeways may remain closed on specific days or during maintenance hours. Evening Ganga Aarti timings vary by season.
Fare includes: Round Trip Travel inclusive of toll tax and parking.

attractions.name: Har Ki Pauri (Ganga Aarti)
attractions.text: Har Ki Pauri is the most sacred ghat in Haridwar and the spiritual centre of the city. Devotees from across the country gather here to take a holy dip in the Ganga and to witness the famous evening Ganga Aarti, when hundreds of lamps float on the river to the sound of bells and chanting. The atmosphere is deeply moving and is the highlight of any Haridwar visit.

attractions.name: Mansa Devi Temple
attractions.text: Perched atop the Bilwa Parvat, Mansa Devi Temple is dedicated to Goddess Mansa Devi, who is believed to fulfil the wishes of her devotees. The temple can be reached by a scenic cable car ride that offers panoramic views of Haridwar and the Ganga. It is one of the most visited shrines in the city.

attractions.name: Chandi Devi Temple
attractions.text: Located on the Neel Parvat on the banks of the Ganga, Chandi Devi Temple is an important Siddh Peeth dedicated to Goddess Chandi. The temple holds great religious significance and offers beautiful views of the surrounding hills, accessible by foot or by ropeway.

attractions.name: Triveni Ghat (Rishikesh)
attractions.text: Triveni Ghat is the largest and most sacred ghat in Rishikesh, believed to be the confluence of three holy rivers — the Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati. Pilgrims come here for a holy bath and to attend the serene Maha Aarti held on the riverbank. It is a peaceful spot to soak in the spiritual energy of Rishikesh.

attractions.name: Laxman Jhula & Ram Jhula
attractions.text: Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula are the iconic suspension bridges of Rishikesh that span the Ganga and connect the temples and ashrams on either bank. Surrounded by riverside cafés, temples and markets, these bridges offer stunning views of the river and the hills and are among the most photographed landmarks in Rishikesh.

attractions.name: Parmarth Niketan Ashram
attractions.text: Parmarth Niketan is the largest ashram in Rishikesh, known for its tranquil setting on the banks of the Ganga and its world-famous evening Ganga Aarti. The ashram is a centre for yoga and meditation and welcomes visitors seeking peace and spirituality.

attractions.name: Amber Fort (Amer Fort)
attractions.text: Majestic fort located on a hilltop with sweeping views. Famous for its artistic Hindu architecture and the Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace).

attractions.name: City Palace
attractions.text: A beautiful blend of Mughal and Rajput architecture. Houses museums, courtyards, and the royal family’s residence.

attractions.name: Nahargarh Fort
attractions.text: Perched on a ridge of the Aravalli Hills, this fort offers breathtaking panoramic views of the entire Jaipur city, especially at sunset. It was a formidable defense post and is known for the stunning architecture within, including twelve identical boudoirs for the king’s queens.

attractions.name: Jantar Mantar
attractions.text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest and best-preserved astronomical observatories in the world. Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, who was a scholar of astronomy, it houses a collection of 19 large instruments, including the world’s largest stone sundial.

attractions.name: Jal Mahal (Water Palace)
attractions.text: A beautiful low-rise palace that appears to float in the middle of the Man Sagar Lake, making it a picturesque sight.

attractions.name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
attractions.text: Arguably the most iconic landmark of the city, this five-story palace was built in 1799. Its unique honeycomb-like facade has 953 small windows (jharokhas), which allowed the royal ladies to observe the bus street life below without being seen themselves.

attractions.name: Birla Mandir, Jaipur
attractions.text: Dedicated to Lord Vishnu (Narayan) and his consort Goddess Lakshmi, this modern temple is often referred to as the Laxmi Narayan Temple. It is part of a series of grand temples built by the wealthy Birla family across India.

Near to this place, you will also find markets flooded with krishna idols, his accessories. introParas: Embark on an unforgettable spiritual journey with this 3 days Mathura Govardhan Agra tour. This Mathura Govardhan Agra tour package traces the divine footsteps of Lord Krishna across Braj Bhumi, from his birthplace in Mathura and childhood home in Gokul to Vrindavan, the Govardhan Parikrama, and the villages of Nandgaon and Barsana, before ending with the Taj Mahal in Agra. It offers a rich experience of Hindu mythology, spirituality, and the timeless love story of Radha and Krishna, set amidst the picturesque landscapes of Uttar Pradesh.

itinerary.title: Delhi to Mathura
paras: Our Driver will come to pick you from Delhi early in the morning then drive for Mathura – the birth place of Lord Krishna”. On Arrival, check in hotel and proceed towards Gokul, at 15 km distance from Mathura. Visit Gokulnath Temple, Nand Bhawan, Raman Reti and soak in the serene atmosphere of this quaint town. The Gokul city is situated on the banks of River Yamuna and is quite crowded during the festivals of Krishna Janmashtami and Nandotsav. After Sightseeing in Gokul Drive back to Mathura.

Mathura is a sacred city in Uttar Pradesh, northern India. The deity Lord Krishna is said to have been born on the site of Sri Krishna Janma Bhoomi, a Hindu temple. Dotting the Yamuna River are 25 ghats (flights of steps down to the water), of which Vishram Ghat is considered the holiest. Sati Burj is a 16th-century memorial tower. Dwarkadhish Temple has a carved entrance and a black-marble idol of Lord Krishna.

After Sightseeing in Mathura in the afternoon, go back to your hotel for some rest. By late afternoon, proceed to Vrindavan for a splendid tour. Vrindavan is a holy town in Uttar Pradesh, northern India. The Hindu deity Krishna is said to have spent his childhood here. It is home to temples, many dedicated to Krishna and his lover, the deity Radha. At Banke Bihari Temple, the curtain in front of Krishna’s statue is opened and closed every few minutes. At Radha Raman Temple, a gold plate beside Krishna signifies Radha. Prem Mandir is a huge white marble temple. After arrival in Vrindavan, visit Nidhivan, Banke Bihari Temple, Iskcon Temple and in the evening, visit Prem Mandir. Enjoy light and sound show and spend some time in temple premises. Have your dinner and return to Mathura hotel for overnight stay.

paras: After Breakfast Drive towards Govardhan. Mathura to Govardhan distance is 21 km and takes approx. 35 minutes to reach. Upon arrival, you can begin with Govardhan Parikrama. Govardhan Hill, also called Mount Govardhana and Giriraj, is a sacred Hindu site in the Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh, India on an 8 km long hill located in the area of Govardhan and Radha Kund, which is about 21 kilometres from Vrindavan.

After Sightseeing in Govardhan, Drive towards Barsana. Barsana is a historical town and nagar panchayat in the Mathura district of the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. Barsana is believed to be the home of the Hindu goddess Radha, the consort of Krishna. It is in the Braj region. It is located at 27.65°N 77.38°E. The main attraction of the town is Radha Rani Temple also known as Radha Rani Rangili Mahal. Barsana is famous for Lathmaar Holi

Nandgaon is a religious centre in Braj Region near to the State Border of Uttar Pradesh & Rajasthan. It is situated 55 km from Mathura, 10 km from Barsana and 29 km from Govardhan. This place is visited to experience childhood of Shree Krishna spent with his foster parents-Yashoda and Nandbaba. The Taj Mahal, is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in the Indian city of Agra. It was commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal; it also houses the tomb of Shah Jahan himself.

Agra Fort is another highlight where the red sandstone structure tells the story of the Mughal emperors. Itmad-ud-Daulah’s Tomb is also known as “Baby Taj” because of its similar structure. After a day of sightseeing you return to the hotel for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Agra to Mathura and Vrindavan
paras: Morning we leave for Mathura. Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple marks the exact place of his birth and is a pious place. The streets of Mathura are lined with temples and sacred sites that reflects its connection with Lord Krishna. Post lunch we leave for Vrindavan. itinerary.title: Vrindavan to Haridwar – Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri
paras: The tour moves to Haridwar which is one of the most sacred cities of India. On arrival check in to hotel and then visit Mansa Devi Temple which is on a Hill and has a beautiful view of the city. During the time of sunset, the experience of Ganga Aarti at Har Ki Pauri is unforgettable. Thousands of people gather on the ghat to float oil lamps in the holy water. Overnight stay in Haridwar lets you soak in the divinity of the city.

itinerary.title: Haridwar to Rishikesh and Back
paras: On this day early morning ,you will be taken to Rishikesh where you can take a stop at Ram Jhula and Lakshman Jhula suspension bridge which is built over the Ganga river. It is also famous for its spirituality and adventure activities such as River Rafting and Bungee Jumping. Move to Geeta Bhawan for religious discourses and teachings. Apart from that you can also explore famous ashrams such as Parmarth Niketan Ashram, and The Beatles Ashram where yoga and meditation happen. After Rishikesh, you will return back to Haridwar for an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Haridwar to Delhi
